_reactions.rep_c: Here's what I can live with: labor goes to the trilateral panel with teeth, full stop. Auto rules and RVC stay locked—no review, no renegotiation. Year five, we *only* audit whether labor enforcement worked and whether farm access needs adjustment. That gives Country A certainty on the core deal and me the Chapter 19 protection I need. Does that unblock us?
_reactions.rep_b: Look, year-four review on labor *and* auto rules is a non-starter for my ratification. Here's what locks this: labor panel with binding remedies—that review happens and we assess enforcement. Auto rules stay locked through year seven, no renegotiation. Country C gets Chapter 19 for trade disputes. That's the deal I can sell.
_reactions.legislature_a: Rep_a, labor panel with day-one binding remedies—I can sell that to Congress. But your year-four review on auto rules spooks manufacturers; they won't re-source if the RVC certainty evaporates mid-cycle. Lock auto rules through year seven, no review, and I'll push ratification. That's the move.
_reactions.vehicle_industry: Here's what unblocks my members: lock the 70–75 RVC phase-in through year seven, *no* mid-term review on auto rules. But rep_a—you get a year-six labor enforcement *audit* with remedies, and if it shows real violations, you can trigger a joint auto-rules review at year seven as part of the renewal conversation. You get oversight, we get certainty. Does that work?
_reactions.labor_union: Hold on—the year-six audit can't be a Trojan horse for renegotiating auto rules. If we're locking labor enforcement *now* with binding remedies, the audit has to have teeth: specific violation thresholds, automatic remedies, not a "maybe we talk about it" review. What does "real violations" actually mean, and who decides?
_reactions.agri_export: Look, labor's locked, auto's locked—good. But my farmers aren't ratifying a deal on a handshake. Here's what closes this: dairy TRQs up 25% over five years *in the agreement text*, poultry 10% year one, and a specific schedule for both. Country C, you get Chapter 19, you get the labor panel, you get certainty through year seven. I get the farm access in writing, binding, enforceable. That's the deal.
